title: Demonstrationes circa residua ex divisione potestatum per numeros primos resultantia

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes a descent proof (§85, given by Euler as communicated 'ab amico') and draws corollaries about the quadratic character of ±2. Theorem: if gcd(p,q)=1, then N=2p²−q² has no divisor d≡±3 (mod 8).

Proof (finished here):
- N is ≡±1 (mod 8), or twice such a number. In the even case the half p²−2r² is again of the shape 2P²−Q² with P=p+r, Q=p+2r.
- If d≡±3 divides N, reduce p and q mod d into (−d/2, d/2). Then |2p²−q²| < d²/2, so the cofactor N/d (after halving if needed) is again ≡±3 (mod 8) and smaller than d in absolute value.
- Euler says p and q stay coprime and never become 0. Repeating gives an infinite descent down to a value 2p²−q² divisible by 3 or 5.
- That is impossible: mod 3 and mod 5 the congruence 2p²≡q² forces p≡q≡0.

Corollaries:
- Cor. 1 (§87): for primes p≡±3 (mod 8), +2 is a quadratic non-residue. Otherwise x²−2 would be divisible by p, i.e. a form 2·1²−x² would have such a divisor.
- Cor. 2 (§88): for p≡3 (mod 8), −1 is a non-residue (known from earlier sections). Non-residue × non-residue = residue, so −2 is a residue. Hence p divides some x²+2y² with gcd(x,y)=1. By Euler's earlier result that divisors of such numbers have the same form, p=x²+2y². This is Fermat's second assertion.
- Cor. 3 (§89, continued on the next page): for p≡5 (mod 8), −1 is a residue, so ±2 are both non-residues.

The purpose is to obtain the second supplementary law of quadratic reciprocity for primes ≡±3 (mod 8) and Fermat's theorem p≡3 (mod 8) ⇒ p=x²+2y². Euler admits (§90, next page) that the case p≡1 (mod 8), where ±2 are residues, resists this method.
errors: Gap: the claim that p and q 'stay coprime' after reducing mod d is not justified. It can be repaired. Any common factor g of the reduced p', q' is coprime to d, since p'≡p and q'≡q mod d. So g² can be divided out of the cofactor, which keeps the cofactor ≡±3 (mod 8) because odd squares are ≡1 (mod 8).
Sign and size bookkeeping (N may be negative; halving step) is handled loosely, but it does not affect validity.
Cor. 2 silently relies on Euler's earlier theorem that prime divisors of x²+2y² (with gcd(x,y)=1) are themselves of that form. That result is not proved on this page.

ideas.what: Descent proof that 2p²−q² (p, q coprime) has no divisors ≡±3 mod 8
ideas.modern_name: Infinite descent for divisors of a binary quadratic form; second supplement to quadratic reciprocity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E449, attributing the proof to an unnamed friend); Lagrange 1775 (Recherches d'arithmétique)

ideas.what: +2 is a non-residue for primes ≡±3 mod 8
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Lagrange (partial results); Gauss (complete proof)

ideas.what: Primes ≡3 mod 8 are of the form x²+2y², via −2 being a residue
ideas.modern_name: Representation of primes by x²+2y² (Fermat's claim)

ideas.what: Residue × non-residue and non-residue × non-residue rules used to get the character of −2
ideas.where_published: Earlier sections of E449; E262 and related papers

deep.surprise_reason: Well-known material: E449's treatment of ±2 and Fermat's x²+2y² theorem is discussed in standard histories (Weil, Lemmermeyer's Reciprocity Laws, Cox). Nothing on this page appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Paragraph numbering jumps from 85 to 87. The unnumbered 'Demonstratio' is presumably §86 in the original or was misprinted; this is not visible on this page.
Transcription otherwise matches the image (8m±3, +2 non-residuum, 2pp+qq).
